1 
 
 
June 15, 2026 
 
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
Department of Health and Human Services  
Attention: CMS–0062–P 
 (Submitted electronically to www.regulations.gov) 
 
Re: 
CMS-0062-P – Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs for 
Medicare Advantage, Medicaid Managed Care, CHIP and QHPs on Federally-Facilitated 
Exchanges 
 
On behalf of SS&C Health, the following represents our comments to the April 14, 2026 referenced 
Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) Interoperability Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs, 
issued by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. 
 
SS&C Health provides healthcare and pharmacy solution claims software, analytics and outsourced 
claims processing services to health plans across the U.S.  Our clients include health plans or third party 
administrators; utilizing SS&C claims platforms and/or staff to provide coverage to approximately 52 
million lives, including 24 million individuals in Medicare Advantage, Medicaid or Federal Exchange 
health plans covered by the NPRM. Although we provide technology and service solutions to some large 
plans, the bulk of our client base are mid-sized and small plans, with 32,000 to 500,000 enrollees.  
Included in our health technology and outsourcing services is a FHIR based Interoperability solution to 
meet the Patient Access API under the 2020 CMS Interoperability and Patient Access rule, and a 
developing solution to meet the Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs in 2027.    
 
Comments Regarding Proposed Rule’s October 1, 2027 Implementation Dates for Specific Components 
of CMS-0062  
 
Section 42 CFR 422.119(b)(1)(v) of the proposed regulation, covering Medicare Advantage plans, along 
with identical language in Parts 431 and for Medicaid, 457 for CHIP and 45 CFR Part 156 for Federal 
Exchange, would require impacted payers to add information about prior authorization for prescription 
drugs to their Patient Access. Provider Access and Payer to Payer APIs, effective October 1, 2027.   The 
prescription drug prior authorization data added to the three APIs includes authorization status, date 
approved or denied, end date of authorization, dosage, reason if denied, and clinical information from 
provider.  The proposed rule would additionally require Medicare Advantage plans at 42 CFR 
422.119(c)(2) to adhere to HL7 FHIR Provider Data Exchange (PDex) Implementation Guide for clinical 
data, effective October 1, 2027 (with identical language applying PDex in Parts 431 for Medicaid, 457 for 
CHIP and 45 CFR Part 156 for Federal Exchange). 
 
Conflicting Implementation Timeline with Existing FHIR API Mandates 
The proposed date for adding data from prescription drug prior authorization requests to the Patient 
Access, Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs is aggressive considering other new FHIR API initiatives 
impacted plans will be implementing for 2027.  Additional API requirements for impacted plans to 
comply with during the second half of 2027, specifically a new category of data from prescription drug 
prior authorizations and adherence to additional HL7 standards, when plans have just established 3 new 
API data exchanges with providers and other plans poses risks that could undermine implementations of 
both 2024 CMS-0057 prior authorization API final rule and this proposed CMS-0062 rule’s requirements.   
 
2 
 
 
The risk is based on experience to date with our impacted plan clients, given that nearly all of our 
client’s provider system and other health plan partners have not initiated or even scheduled testing and 
connectivity with the new 2027 APIs, or are even prepared to accept data via the APIs.  We therefore 
expect external parties to engage in a gradual testing, connectivity and implementation of the CMS-
0057 requirements running well into, and even past 2027.  Adding new categories of data and additional 
standards in mid-2027 during the ongoing implementation and corrections of API data exchanges 
between plans and providers to meet the CMS-0057 final rule poses risks that neither of the two 
regulatory initiatives will be effectively executed.  Recent history from implementation of the Patient 
Access API supports this expected implantation dynamic, when most plans experienced gradual 
engagement from third party applications months or years after the July 2021 deadline for establishing 
the API occurred. 
 
Challenge for Payers to Convert Data to Proposed Mandated FHIR Standards within Timeline  
The requirement in the proposed rule that impacted payers conform their clinical data, from both the 
existing CMS-0057 requirement on medical prior authorizations and the proposed 0062 rule’s mandate 
on pharmacy prior authorizations, to the HL7 FHIR PDex Implementation Guide starting October 1, 2027 
will be a compliance challenge.  Clinical data is the most difficult of all data types subject to the various 
FHIR API requirements to convert to FHIR.  Unlike medical claims data subject to X12 837 standard and 
drug claims data subject to NCPDP standard, there are no industry standards for health plans to transact 
clinical data.  In addition, clinical data comes in a variety of formats, such as text, PDFs, images, charts 
and other attachments.  The proposed rules mandate for impacted plans to conform to PDex in October 
2027 will require plans to make extensive changes to data and attachment mapping, months after they 
have already made the clinical data available to meet the January 2027 requirement.  Our experience 
working with clients is that this will create a significant conversion burden on plans, as well as a 
considerable change for providers to ingest the new standard.  In addition, this new standard mandate is 
proposed to take effect during the challenging gradual adoption environment during 2027, outlined in 
the previous paragraph. 
 
Given these two areas of concern, SS&C Health recommends CMS delay the requirements that impacted 
payers add information about prior authorization requests and decisions to the Patient and Provider 
Access, and Payer-to-Payer FHIR APIs, and support the HL7 FHIR PDex Implementation Guide for clinical 
data made available via the FHIR APIs until July 2028.   
 
Thank you for your consideration of SS&C Health’s comments on the NPRM.  I invite any further 
questions, comments or discussions, as you deem appropriate.  Please direct any communications 
regarding this response to:  
 
Richard Popper  
richard.popper@sscinc.com    410-294-8215 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Mark Cone 
Vice President and Chief Compliance Officer  
SS&C Health 
Mark Cone

# Comment Analysis Template: CMS-2026-1255-0001

## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** Mark Cone, Vice President and Chief Compliance Officer, SS&C Health; contact Richard Popper.
- **Stakeholder type:** Technology Vendor / outsourced claims processing vendor.
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** SS&C Health provides healthcare/pharmacy claims software, analytics, outsourced claims processing, and FHIR interoperability solutions for health plans covering about 52 million lives, including 24 million lives in programs affected by the rule; many clients are mid-sized and small plans.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

SS&C Health focuses on the proposed October 1, 2027 implementation date for adding prescription drug PA data to Patient Access, Provider Access, and Payer-to-Payer APIs and requiring PDex for clinical data. The commenter argues the timeline conflicts with implementation of existing 2024 API mandates and recommends delaying these requirements until July 2028.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; PA-DRUG-PHARMACY; FHIR-IG-REQUIRED; ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE; API-USAGE-METRICS/related API data reporting; GENERAL timeline implementation.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** 42 CFR 422.119(b)(1)(v), 42 CFR 422.119(c)(2), Parts 431, 457, and 45 CFR Part 156.
- **Standards referenced:** HL7 FHIR PDex Implementation Guide, FHIR APIs, X12 837, NCPDP.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Conflict with existing 2027 API implementation**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED; PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Modify.
- **Rationale:** Impacted payers will already be standing up major CMS-0057 API capabilities in 2027. SS&C expects providers and other payer partners to test and connect gradually, potentially into and beyond 2027.
- **Specific request:** Delay the requirement to add prescription drug prior authorization data to Patient Access, Provider Access, and Payer-to-Payer APIs until July 2028.

**Topic 2: PDex clinical data conversion burden**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED; ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE
- **Position:** Modify.
- **Rationale:** Clinical data is difficult to convert to FHIR because it lacks the transaction standardization of claims data and appears in text, PDFs, images, charts, and attachments. Requiring PDex by October 2027 would force extensive remapping soon after initial January 2027 API builds.
- **Specific request:** Delay required support for HL7 FHIR PDex for clinical data made available via the FHIR APIs until July 2028.

**Topic 3: Small and mid-sized plan readiness**
- **Provision ID:** SMALL-PAYER-IMPACT; TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY
- **Position:** Modify.
- **Rationale:** SS&C serves many mid-sized and small plans that depend on vendor implementation capacity and trading partner readiness. The proposed timing may be particularly difficult for plans with limited resources.
- **Specific request:** Provide additional time to reduce risk to both CMS-0057 and CMS-0062 implementation success.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S1/S2/S3/S37:** Addresses mandatory IG/version implementation by objecting to the October 2027 PDex timing and requesting a July 2028 delay.
- **S21:** Argues the October 1, 2027 timeline for drug PA API data is not achievable alongside existing 2027 API mandates.
- **S47/S50/S53/S54:** By implication, recommends a phased/delayed schedule, citing testing, conformance, and readiness concerns.
- **S60-S65:** Addresses standards adoption/versioning through concern that PDex clinical-data conformance is too difficult to require in October 2027.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Delay adding prescription drug PA request and decision information to the Patient Access API, Provider Access API, and Payer-to-Payer API until July 2028.
2. Delay required support for the HL7 FHIR PDex IG for clinical data in these APIs until July 2028.
3. Avoid layering new drug PA data categories and standards during the same period when plans, providers, and other payers are still testing and correcting CMS-0057 API implementations.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** October 1, 2027 implementation date, overlapping CMS-0057 implementation, provider/trading partner unreadiness, clinical data conversion burden.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Undermined implementation of both CMS-0057 and CMS-0062, compliance challenges, disruptions in API rollout, provider ingestion problems.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Trading partner testing delays, lack of standards for payer clinical data, heterogeneous attachment formats, data mapping complexity, small/mid-sized plan resource constraints.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** SS&C states it serves clients covering about 52 million lives, including 24 million in affected government/Exchange plans; many clients have 32,000 to 500,000 enrollees.
- **Studies or research referenced:** No formal studies cited.
- **Examples provided:** Experience with Patient Access API adoption after July 2021, where third-party app engagement occurred gradually over months or years; current clients' provider and payer partners have not initiated/scheduled API testing.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Health plans, third-party administrators, providers, other payers, technology vendors, small and mid-sized plans.
- **Economic implications:** Additional build and remapping costs; potential wasted effort if implementation changes occur before initial API adoption stabilizes.
- **Technical feasibility:** Feasible with additional time; risky under October 2027 timing due to clinical data conversion and partner readiness.
- **Patient care impact:** Not directly discussed, but delayed or unstable interoperability implementation could reduce effectiveness of prior authorization reform.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Concerned / narrowly opposed to timeline.
- **Tone:** Technical, concise, professional.
- **Priority level:** High.

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "The proposed date for adding data from prescription drug prior authorization requests...is aggressive considering other new FHIR API initiatives impacted plans will be implementing for 2027." - Context: Main timeline objection.
2. "Clinical data is the most difficult of all data types subject to the various FHIR API requirements to convert to FHIR." - Context: PDex conversion burden.
3. "SS&C Health recommends CMS delay...until July 2028." - Context: Specific requested compliance date.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - The comment is primarily a request to delay from October 2027 to July 2028.
- [x] **COST-RESOURCES** - Discusses implementation strain and conversion burden for plans and vendors.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - Highlights clinical data mapping and partner connectivity challenges.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** - Focuses on PDex and FHIR implementation readiness.
- [x] **SMALL-PAYER-IMPACT** - Notes many SS&C clients are small and mid-sized plans.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - Provider and payer partner testing/readiness are central barriers.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** - The commenter is a vendor describing client and vendor implementation realities.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - Addresses transition from existing clinical data formats and claims standards to FHIR/PDex.
